title: Azure Databricks -- clusters, jobs, cost management
exp: Azure Databricks is the direct equivalent of the EMR days -- built by the original Spark creators, deeply integrated with Azure infrastructure.
pts: Databricks workspace: the persistent container for notebooks, clusters, jobs, and data.
All-purpose clusters: interactive/dev, billed while running regardless of activity -- idle timeout matters.

Job clusters: created automatically per scheduled Job run, terminated automatically on completion -- the Databricks equivalent of a transient EMR cluster with auto-terminate, and the correct choice for production.

autotermination_minutes on all-purpose clusters is the Databricks equivalent of remembering to terminate an EMR cluster -- except it's set once and forgotten, a genuine safety improvement over the AWS pattern.
Cluster node types map to Azure VM sizes (Standard_DS3_v2, etc.) -- same 'pick based on workload profile' logic as choosing an EC2 instance type.
Two separate cost line items: DBUs (Databricks platform compute-time metric) AND the underlying Azure VM compute -- worth knowing when reasoning about a cost question.
code:
{
  "name": "OrdersPipeline-Daily",
  "new_cluster": {
    "spark_version": "14.3.x-scala2.12",
    "node_type_id": "Standard_DS3_v2",
    "num_workers": 4,
    "autotermination_minutes": 20
  },
  "notebook_task": { "notebook_path": "/Repos/pipeline/validate_and_transform" },
  "timeout_seconds": 3600,
  "max_retries": 1
}

from databricks.sdk import WorkspaceClient
w = WorkspaceClient()
job = w.jobs.create(
    name="OrdersPipeline-Daily",
    tasks=[{"task_key": "validate",
            "new_cluster": {"spark_version": "14.3.x-scala2.12",
                             "node_type_id": "Standard_DS3_v2",
                             "num_workers": 4, "autotermination_minutes": 20},
            "notebook_task": {"notebook_path": "/Repos/pipeline/validate_and_transform"}}]
)

qa.q: Why is a job cluster, not an all-purpose cluster, the correct choice for a scheduled production pipeline?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Job clusters are created fresh for a single Job run and automatically terminated when it completes -- no idle cost risk between runs. All-purpose clusters stay alive (billed) until manually stopped or idle-timeout triggers, and are meant for shared interactive development. This mirrors the exact AWS lesson: use transient EMR clusters with auto-terminate for scheduled batch work, not a persistent cluster.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Cloud control plane APIs orchestrate virtualized hardware, networking (VPC/VNets), IAM policies, and auto-scaling groups.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Overly permissive IAM roles (wildcard actions) or unmonitored resource limits lead to security breaches and unexpected cloud cost spikes.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Serverless/managed services eliminate infrastructure maintenance but introduce cold starts and vendor lock-in.

qa.q: Why does Databricks on Azure show up as two separate cost line items?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** DBUs (the Databricks platform's own compute-time billing unit, covering the runtime and management plane) are billed separately from the underlying Azure VM compute those clusters run on. A slow job isn't automatically an expensive one, or vice versa -- DBU rate varies by cluster type (all-purpose is billed at a higher rate than job clusters for the same VM size), so checking both numbers separately is necessary to actually diagnose a cost question.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Cloud control plane APIs orchestrate virtualized hardware, networking (VPC/VNets), IAM policies, and auto-scaling groups.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Overly permissive IAM roles (wildcard actions) or unmonitored resource limits lead to security breaches and unexpected cloud cost spikes.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Serverless/managed services eliminate infrastructure maintenance but introduce cold starts and vendor lock-in.
